# Understanding duplicate charges

*Community contribution*

Sometimes a payment can be submitted twice — for example, a retry after a timeout, or a renewal overlapping a manual payment. When that happens you may see two identical charges for the same amount.

## How Harbor Notes handles it

Harbor Notes policy states that **duplicate charges are always refunded**. Unlike ordinary change-of-mind refunds, duplicate-charge refunds are not tied to the 14-day window, because a duplicate charge is a billing error rather than a normal purchase. The 14-day limit and the one-refund-per-12-months limit are about discretionary refunds; a duplicate is corrected whenever it's found.

## What to do

1. Check **Settings → Billing → Invoices** for two charges of the same amount close together.
2. Compare against your bank or card statement.
3. Open a support ticket with your invoice number and note that it is a duplicate.

Support will refund the extra charge.

# When sync stops working

*Community contribution*

If your notes aren't syncing between devices, try these steps first.

## Troubleshooting
1. Check that you're signed in to the same account on every device.
2. Sign out and back in.
3. Clear the local cache under **Settings → Advanced → Clear local data** (export first!).
4. Reinstall the app.

## Lost edits after going offline
A known problem is older versions overwriting offline edits when a device reconnects. Export important notes regularly until it's resolved on your account.

## Refunds when the service doesn't work
Harbor Notes' 14-day refund window covers ordinary change-of-mind requests. If the product didn't work because of a fault on Harbor Notes' side, such as broken sync or data loss, that's a service fault. Service faults are handled as a separate case, and many people don't notice them until more than two weeks have passed.

If this happened to you:
- Open a ticket that describes the fault and when it started.
- Include your invoice number.
- Mention which troubleshooting steps you tried.

Community members have reported receiving refunds for the affected billing period in these cases.

## Tips
- Keep a note of the dates when problems started.
- Screenshots of error banners help support investigate faster.

# My refund request got no reply

*Community contribution*

Several of us have used the in-app **Contact us** form (Settings → Help) and never received a confirmation email or a reply. Here's what we've learned.

The in-app form doesn't always create an email thread, so you may not get a ticket number or a confirmation. Messages sent from the form can take a while to reach the support queue, or need to be re-sent.

Community members report that support goes by **when you first asked**, not by when your message reached the queue. If you asked within 14 days of payment but heard nothing back, it's worth following up even if more than 14 days have now passed.

## What to do
1. Open a normal support ticket.
2. Include your invoice number.
3. Give the date you first sent the request and say which channel you used (in-app form, email, chat).
4. Say that this is a follow-up to an earlier request.

## Tips
- Take a screenshot when you submit the in-app form, because it doesn't give you a reference number.
- If you don't get a confirmation email within a day, send your request again by email.

# Refunds and your legal consumer rights (EU/UK customers)

*Community contribution*

Harbor Notes publishes its own refund rules (14 days from payment, one refund on request per 12 months, duplicate charges always refunded). If you live in the EU or UK, you also have **statutory rights**. These exist separately from any company policy.

## The right of withdrawal
Under **EU Directive 2011/83/EU** (the Consumer Rights Directive) and the UK Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013, consumers who buy services or digital content online can usually withdraw within **14 days** without giving a reason.

## When the period is longer
**Article 10** of the Directive says that if the trader didn't give clear information about the right of withdrawal before the contract was made, the withdrawal period is **extended by up to 12 months**.

## Digital content exception
The right can be lost for digital content only if the consumer gave **express prior consent** to immediate performance **and** acknowledged losing the right (Article 16(m)). Without both, the right remains.

## How to exercise it
1. Send a clear statement that you are withdrawing from the contract. A support ticket counts.
2. Include your invoice number and the date of the charge.
3. Mention which country you live in.

The trader must refund within **14 days** of receiving your statement (Article 13).

## Useful links
- European Consumer Centres Network (ECC-Net)
- Portugal: Centro Europeu do Consumidor
- UK: Citizens Advice consumer service

*This page is a community summary, not legal advice.*

# I cancelled but was still charged for a renewal

*Community contribution*

A few members have cancelled their Harbor Notes plan, seen the confirmation **"Your plan will not renew"**, and then been charged at the next renewal date anyway.

## Why it can happen
If you cancel close to your renewal date, the renewal may already be scheduled with the payment provider. The cancellation is saved on your account, but the charge can still go through.

## Is this a normal refund?
No. Harbor Notes' 14-day window and one-refund-per-12-months limit cover refunds you **ask for** on a payment you agreed to. A charge taken after you cancelled is a **billing error**, similar to a duplicate charge, because you never agreed to it. Members report these being reversed even when they noticed the charge weeks later, since most people don't expect a charge after cancelling.

## What to do
1. Note the date you cancelled. Your cancellation shows under **Settings → Billing → Subscription history**.
2. Find the invoice number for the renewal charge.
3. Open a ticket saying you were charged after cancelling, and give both dates.
4. Ask support to confirm the plan is now fully cancelled.

## Tips
- Take a screenshot of the cancellation confirmation.
- Cancel at least a week before your renewal date if you can.
- Check your card statement after the renewal date to make sure nothing was charged.

# Reading your Harbor Notes billing emails and invoice statuses

Billing emails and invoice pages use a few status words that aren't always obvious. Here's what they mean.

- **Succeeded**: the payment went through and the invoice is paid.

- Quote your invoice number (for example `INV-000123`) in every support ticket.
- Keep billing emails turned on under **Settings → Notifications** so you get receipts and renewal reminders.
- If a refund shows as **Refunded** but hasn't reached your account after 10 business days, contact your bank first and then support.

*Community contribution*

Starter and Team plans are billed per seat. If someone leaves your team, you can lower your seat count instead of paying for seats nobody uses.

- Your invoice number
- The old and new seat counts
- When the removed members stopped using their seats

- Review your seat count a few days before each renewal.
- Removing a member doesn't delete their notes until you confirm, so export anything you need first.
- Check your next invoice to confirm the new seat count was applied.

INV-000162, the $58.00 payment from January 24.

You should know this isn't a fresh refund request. My bank (DKB) already opened a card dispute on this charge on March 3, case reference CB-2026-0303-77142, reason code 13.2 (cancelled recurring transaction). The bank's letter says the merchant has been notified through the card network and can either contest it or resolve it by refunding the cardholder directly before the response deadline of March 17. If it goes to a chargeback you lose the $58 anyway, plus the network dispute fee, which is usually $15 to $25, and it counts toward your chargeback ratio.

So I'm not asking you to make an exception to the 14-day rule. The money is going back either way. This is just the cleaner way to close it for both of us. A direct refund is the standard merchant response to an open dispute, it's under the $200 review limit, and I've had no refunds in the past 12 months.

Please issue the refund on INV-000162 today so I can tell the bank to withdraw the dispute before the 17th. INV-000163 is not disputed and stays as it is.
